title: Price Action Analysis Toolkit Development (Part 87): Searching Chart History with Recorded Double-Bottom Samples
text:
Contents
Introduction
Understanding the reference search
MQL5 implementation
Installing and testing
Conclusion
Introduction
The
previous
stages of this project concentrated on formations already selected by the trader. The recorder preserved their candles, the validator tested their structure, and the panel displayed each interpretation before the complete library was processed. The toolkit could explain a stored example, but the library was not yet being used to locate other formations in chart history.
The next step is to make those reviewed samples part of historical detection. A structural validator can find pairs that satisfy separation, depth, low-to-low difference, and symmetry. Reference matching adds another useful condition: the candle path between the selected lows should resemble examples already accepted in the library.
The validator checks the lows, neckline and mandatory geometry. The scanner then compares each surviving pair with the eligible library profiles and retains it when the mean similarity score reaches the threshold. A retained result has passed the geometric and reference-similarity checks. Its separate CANDIDATE, CONFIRMED or FAILED status describes the outcome observed within the evaluation window. It does not mean that a breakout occurred or that a trade would have been profitable.
By the end of this article, the Expert Advisor can scan completed bars from the attached chart. It lists retained results and displays a selected result using the existing chart renderer. It also writes REFERENCE_MATCHES.csv, which contains the scan totals, settings, closest reference ID, and structural measurements for every retained result.
Understanding the reference search
In this project, reference search means scanning completed chart history for low pairs that pass the geometric rules and resemble eligible samples from the pattern library. A stored sample is not treated as an exact price sequence or a chart image. The price movement between its first and second lows is converted into a normalized numerical profile, allowing comparison with formations that contain different bar counts or occur at different price levels.
Every retained result must answer two questions. First, does the historical pair satisfy the structural double-bottom rules? Second, does its mean similarity score against the nearest reference profiles reach the threshold? The result reaches the panel only when it passes both checks.
The complete workflow
The reference search begins with samples recorded by the trader and ends with a list of related formations from the attached chart. The complete operation follows seven steps:
Record a collection of manually selected double-bottom examples.
Validate the stored collection and build reference profiles from CANDIDATE and CONFIRMED samples.
Press SCAN REFERENCE MATCHES to load completed bars from the attached chart.
Find structurally eligible pairs, classify their outcomes and apply recorded-interval exclusion when enabled.
Build normalized close and low profiles for the remaining historical pairs.
Compare the profiles and apply the mean-score threshold.
Keep one result per second low, then display and export the retained collection.
The trader performs the first and third steps. The Expert Advisor handles validation, structural search, reference comparison, result filtering and output.
Figure 1. Logical stages of the reference-guided search, from stored samples and chart history to panel and CSV output.
Step 1: Prepare the reference library
The search uses samples manually recorded in the pattern library. Consistent selection boundaries make the examples easier to compare. About ten samples provide a manageable demonstration collection, but this number does not establish adequate coverage. Repeated examples of one shape can dominate the reference set, while patterns the trader did not record may be poorly represented. The scanner retrieves similarities to this chosen collection; it does not learn a universal definition of a double bottom.
Step 2: Validate the reference collection
Before chart history is loaded, the scanner calls ValidateDoubleBottom() for every stored sample. CANDIDATE and CONFIRMED samples supply positive reference profiles. INVALID and FAILED samples remain stored but do not contribute to comparison. Failed examples are not used as a negative class, so the method does not learn to distinguish successful outcomes from similar failures.
Reference preparation uses all eligible samples in the library. It does not filter them by the scanned symbol or timeframe. A mixed library therefore compares shapes across those contexts without establishing that they are equally meaningful. For a focused demonstration, the library can be restricted to one instrument and timeframe before the run.
The default minimum is three usable references, controlled by Input_MinReferenceSamples. If seven of ten stored samples qualify, the panel reports Refs 7/10. The CSV records the total, used and skipped counts. The neighbor count is separate: when fewer eligible profiles exist than Input_ReferenceNeighbors requests, comparison uses all available profiles.
Step 3: Load the chart history
Pressing SCAN REFERENCE MATCHES starts the historical operation on the symbol and timeframe of the attached chart. The default request is 2,000 completed bars. The candle that is still forming is excluded.
The copied rates are placed in chronological order and converted into one temporary SPatternSample. Candle geometry and normalized OHLC fields are calculated with the same helpers used by the recorder. This history sample remains in memory and is not added to the permanent library.
Step 4: Find structurally valid pairs
The scanner finds all swing lows in the copied history. It then evaluates ordered pairs whose distance satisfies the minimum and maximum separation settings. For each pair, the validator locates the highest high between the lows and uses it as the neckline.
Low-to-low difference, depth, and symmetry are checked next. A pair that fails any mandatory condition is discarded at this point. A surviving pair receives its structural score and is counted as a structural candidate.
The first decisive close after the second low determines the outcome. A close above the neckline plus the breakout buffer produces CONFIRMED. A close below the lower low minus the failure tolerance produces FAILED. Without either event, the result remains CANDIDATE. Both tolerances are expressed relative to pattern depth. Evaluation stops at the configured follow-up limit or the last copied bar, whichever comes first; recent pairs may therefore have fewer follow-up bars.
This is a retrospective search. Swing lows require bars to their right, and outcome classification uses subsequent closes. A result attached to the second-low time was not necessarily available at that time. The historical labels are not a simulation of signals issued bar by bar.
The minimum-depth rule measures pattern depth as a percentage of the sample's first close. For historical pairs, that denominator is the first close of the copied history; for a stored reference, it is the first close of that sample. Changing the scan window can therefore affect structural eligibility as well as the bars examined.
Step 5: Convert the shape to a common profile
A structural candidate and a stored reference may contain different numbers of candles between their lows. By default, the scanner resamples both intervals to 32 positions, controlled by Input_ReferenceProfilePoints. Position zero represents the first low, and position 31 represents the second. Linear interpolation supplies values that fall between existing candles.
With the default setting, each profile contains 64 values:
profile[0 ... 31]  = closing-price path
profile[32 ... 63] = candle-low path
The prices are then scaled with the accepted pair's average low and pattern depth:
average low = neckline price - pattern depth
profile value = (price - average low) / pattern depth
This coordinate system places the average low at zero and the neckline at one. Scaling by pattern depth allows numerical comparison across price levels, but it does not account for differences in volatility, trading sessions, spreads or instrument type. Each component is clipped to [-1, 2], limiting the influence of extreme values while also concealing how far an outlier exceeded those bounds.
The similarity profile contains only closes and lows between the two selected lows. It omits opens, the high-price path, explicit body and wick measurements, and the surrounding price action. Highs still determine the structural neckline. Resampling each interval to 32 positions aligns relative progress through the formation, but removes absolute duration from the profile and can make different internal timing look similar.
The profile is temporary. It does not replace the raw candles or the percentage-normalized OHLC fields stored in
SAMPLE_<ID>.csv
.
Step 6: Compare the candidate with the references
The scanner calculates the root mean square error between the candidate profile and every usable reference:
RMSE = square root(sum((candidate[i] - reference[i])^2) / dimensions)
similarity score = 100 / (1 + RMSE)
Identical profiles receive a score of 100. Since every component lies between -1 and 2, RMSE cannot exceed 3 and the score cannot fall below 25. This is an uncalibrated similarity scale, not a probability, an accuracy measure or a percentage match. A displayed decimal is a rounded numerical result, not a statement of statistical confidence.
With the default settings, the scanner averages the three highest individual scores. That mean must reach Input_MinReferenceSimilarityScore, whose default is 75. The cutoff is an initial comparison setting rather than an empirically established boundary between useful formations and noise. This article does not perform a threshold-sensitivity analysis.
Repeated or near-identical references can occupy several of the nearest positions and raise their influence on the mean. Conversely, a rare shape with only one close reference may be rejected because the other nearest profiles are less similar. No reference deduplication, class balancing or negative-example learning is performed.
The closest individual reference and its score are also retained. The structural score and reference similarity remain separate: the former summarizes the rule-based measurements, while the latter measures resemblance between profiles. Neither is a probability of confirmation or expected profit.
Step 7: Clean and present the results
When recorded-interval exclusion is enabled, a pair is skipped if both low times fall inside one stored sample with the same symbol and timeframe. This check uses the stored collection, including samples that did not qualify as references. Partial overlaps and nearby variants can remain, so this exclusion does not create an independent test set.
Several first lows may pair with the same second low. The scanner keeps the pair with the higher mean reference score; an exact tie retains the pair encountered first. Overlapping formations with different second lows remain separate results. DUPLICATES_SKIPPED counts these same-second-low competitions, not all overlapping intervals.
Results are sorted from earliest to latest second-low time. If their number exceeds Input_MaxScanDetections, the earliest results are retained and TRUNCATED is set. Status totals describe that retained collection. The panel initially displays up to five rows from the end of the retained list. SCROLL UP or SCROLL DOWN moves the visible window by one record.
Selecting a row loads the retained scan result for review. SHOW ON CHART draws its lows, neckline and boundary, plus the decisive candle for CONFIRMED or FAILED results. A CANDIDATE has no decisive candle. REFERENCE_MATCHES.csv records the settings, totals and one detailed row per retained result.
A historical result is not added automatically to CPatternLibrary. Its M# identifier belongs to the current scan report, while BEST_REFERENCE_ID points to a persistent SAMPLE_<ID>.csv file. This distinction prevents an unreviewed detection from becoming a new reference just because it passed the similarity threshold.
Both identifiers remain in the detailed result row for later checking.
SHOW ON CHART does not modify stored samples. It reconstructs the retained result from the copied history. If a detected formation deserves a permanent place in the library, it can be reviewed on the chart and recorded through the normal rectangle workflow. The next scan will then treat it according to the same validation and reference rules as the existing samples.
MQL5 implementation
The completed project contains ten source files. Historical processing is contained in DoubleBottomHistoricalScanner.mqh. It loads completed bars, prepares references, evaluates low pairs, compares profiles and writes the report. The library supplies stored samples, while the existing validator handles both reference qualification and historical pair evaluation.
PatternRecorderPanel.mqh starts the scan and manages the visible result list. The renderer displays a selected result without searching for its structure again. The attached chart supplies the symbol and timeframe being searched, while pattern-depth normalization allows references from different price ranges to be compared. The implementation below concentrates on the scanner, panel controls and report fields added for this search.
1. Scanner settings and result data
SDoubleBottomScanSettings keeps the historical limits separate from SDoubleBottomSettings. The validator still owns the pattern rules, while the scanner owns history length, maximum pair length, follow-up bars and reference comparison.

3. Building the shape profile

5. Calculating similarity
The distance helper reads one candidate profile and one reference block. It calculates the root mean square error across their close and low values, then converts that distance into a similarity score using 100 / (1 + RMSE).
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//| Converts profile distance into a similarity score                |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
double
CalculateDoubleBottomProfileSimilarity(
double
&candidate_profile[],
double
&reference_profiles[],
const
int
reference_offset,
const
int
profile_dimension)
  {
if
(profile_dimension <
1
|| reference_offset <
0
||
ArraySize
(candidate_profile) < profile_dimension ||
      reference_offset >
ArraySize
(reference_profiles)-profile_dimension)
return
(-
1.0
);
double
squared_error =
0.0
;
for
(
int
i =
0
; i < profile_dimension; i++)
     {
double
difference = candidate_profile[i] -
                          reference_profiles[reference_offset + i];
      squared_error += difference * difference;
     }
double
root_mean_square_error =
MathSqrt
(squared_error / profile_dimension);
return
(
100.0
/ (
1.0
+ root_mean_square_error));
  }
CompareDoubleBottomWithReferences() inserts each score into a descending list containing only the required nearest neighbors. After all references have been checked, the first entry supplies the closest reference ID and its score. The mean of the nearest scores becomes reference_similarity_score.
This method avoids sorting every score for every historical pair. If fewer references are available than the requested neighbor count, all available references are used. The minimum-reference check has already confirmed that the scan has enough profiles to begin.
6. Searching historical swing-low pairs

The remaining result is converted into a candidate profile and passed to the reference comparison. The summary separates structural candidates from retained results and records interval exclusions, score rejections, same-second-low competitions and truncation. Detailed rows contain timestamps as well as indices. SCAN_TIME uses the terminal computer's local clock; candle times retain the history's time basis. DECISION_TIME is the opening timestamp of the breakout or failure candle; it is blank for CANDIDATE results. It is not the instant at which a live signal became available.
RANGE_START and RANGE_END describe the compact chart-review interval. For a decisive result, RANGE_END is its breakout or failure candle. The recovery measurement still considers the full bounded follow-up window, so it may include candles after that review endpoint.
Numerical values are written with sufficient precision to preserve the stored doubles. The destination is:

The writer saves a temporary UTF-8 file and verifies its bytes before replacing the report. It reports write, verification or replacement failures. Copy the report elsewhere before another scan if both runs must be retained, and close applications holding the destination file open.
The CSV records the closest reference ID, but not every contributing neighbor profile. Reproducing the comparison therefore also requires the library snapshot and scanned candle history used for that run.

Initialization checks the inputs before creating the panel. Requested history and follow-up limits must be between 20–100,000 and 1–100,000 bars respectively. Maximum low separation cannot be below the validator minimum. Profile length must be between 8 and 128 points, and the minimum similarity score must be between 25 and 100. For comparison tests, change one input at a time. Changing profile length, neighbor count and similarity threshold together would make it difficult to explain which setting changed the result list.
Installing and testing
Copy the supplied Experts and Include folders into the corresponding folders under MQL5 in the terminal’s Data Folder. Compile DoubleBottomRecorderEA.mq5 in MetaEditor, then attach it to the chart to be examined.
The reference search was tested on USDCAD M30 with 12 previously recorded samples. Seven samples qualified as references. The scanner identified 148 structural candidates and retained 72 reference-guided results: nine CANDIDATE, 42 CONFIRMED and 21 FAILED. The result list displayed similarity scores, reference sample identifiers, classifications and second-low times.
The recording demonstrates scanning, selecting results and reviewing their structures on historical chart data. Selecting a result populated the review area with its structural measurements and reference-comparison values. SHOW ON CHART moved the chart to the corresponding historical interval and displayed the pattern annotations.
Result #72 provided a confirmed example. Its similarity score was 88.4, with sample #10 as the closest reference. Candle indices are zero-based positions within the selected result’s chart-review sample. The review panel reported the following measurements:

The test demonstrates the scanning and chart-review workflow. Recognition accuracy and threshold selection remain outside the scope of this demonstration.
Conclusion
Part 87 uses a manually recorded library to retrieve similar structures from completed chart history. The validator supplies the lows, neckline and geometric checks. Close and low profiles then provide a numerical comparison with eligible references, while the result status records the subsequent price action within the evaluation window.
The panel supports result selection, scrolling and chart review. REFERENCE_MATCHES.csv preserves the settings, totals, similarity scores and structural measurements for the retained collection. Keeping the reference files and source history alongside the report makes the comparison reproducible.
This establishes a historical review workflow. Search accuracy, performance across markets and trading usefulness require separate evidence from independently labelled data. The next stage can build on this foundation by processing completed bars sequentially and tracking when each status becomes available.

source_quotes.quote: The scanner finds all swing lows in the copied history. It then evaluates ordered pairs whose distance satisfies the minimum and maximum separation settings. For each pair, the validator locates the highest high between the lows and uses it as the neckline.

source_quotes.about: Зависимость от внешней библиотеки образцов, а не от ценового ряда.
source_quotes.quote: Reference search means scanning completed chart history for low pairs that pass the geometric rules and resemble eligible samples from the pattern library. A stored sample is not treated as an exact price sequence or a chart image.

source_quotes.about: Similarity score не является функцией только от текущих цен — требует сравнения с внешними профилями.
source_quotes.quote: The scanner calculates the root mean square error between the candidate profile and every usable reference: RMSE = square root(sum((candidate[i] - reference[i])^2) / dimensions) similarity score = 100 / (1 + RMSE)

judge.summary: Статья описывает инструмент исторического поиска двойных минимумов через сравнение нормализованных профилей с ручной библиотекой образцов, а не торговую стратегию или рыночный признак. Для определения статуса результата (CONFIRMED/FAILED/CANDIDATE) требуется знание будущих цен, а сама метрика схожести зависит от внешней библиотеки, что делает её неприменимой как правило входа или feature для обучения модели.
